business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mobile Utility Software and Device Performance Optimization Apps

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Quebec Civil Law for private and commercial matters, with federal Common Law for public and tax matters
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46. Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Regulation respecting the register of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1; Civil Code of Quebec, articles 2236-2238 applicable to société en commandite; Charte de la langue française, CQLR c C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document for each general partner and every beneficial owner exceeding the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of country of origin or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Apostille Convention states; otherwise Consular Legalization via the embassy/consulate of Canada or the state where the document was notarized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Legal Existence for any corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency listing directors and officers of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate secretary of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized declaration of beneficial ownership (UBO declaration) in form prescribed by the Quebec Registrar of Enterprises
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in Quebec or foreign notary duly authenticated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial authentication followed by Apostille for foreign Quebec-bound documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing a representative or agent for service in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each limited partner or general partner executing the document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified general partners, limited partners, directors, officers, and UBOs against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, and applicable domestic law enforcement watchlists. Political Exposure checks are mandatory; any foreign PEP triggers Enhanced Due Diligence requirements under FINTRAC guidance, including source-of-funds verification and senior management approval. Re-screening is required within 90 days and upon any material change in ownership or the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises (CLIC portal at www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, the name of a limited partnership must be in French; a French-language form is mandatory unless the name is a recognized trademark. Where transliteration is needed, names must be rendered in the Latin alphabet and comply with the linguistic norms respecting accents and typography; the name must include or be accompanied by 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' in legal French naming convention.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar reserves the name or rejects an application, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration within 30 days after the refusal decision, providing legal submissions and alternative name options. If reconsideration is refused, the decision may be appealed to the Tribunal administratif du Québec within 30 days of the notice of refusal. During the appeal, a new name reservation or amended declaration may be filed without penalty if the appeal is grounded on a typographical or administrative error.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally permissible for the registered office of a Quebec limited partnership in the technology and software development sector, provided the address is a real physical location in Quebec where legal mail and notices may be served during regular business hours. The virtual office provider must accept service of process and maintain a contact person. A purely virtual address without a designated agent is not permissible. No local employee or substantive office space is required solely for an ISIC 6201 mobile utility app developer, but the registered office must be disclosed in the Register of Enterprises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximated at 7% cumulative annual probability for this sector, rising to 35% if the entity holds bank accounts in Quebec, receives grants or tax credits, or has demonstrated irregularities in annual declarations. Unannounced physical inspections are normally triggered by complaints, inconsistent registry data, or a credible UBO mismatch.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille fees for identity bundle (passports, UBO declaration, power of attorney) for foreign signatories

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Professional registered agent / virtual office provider in Quebec

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), arts. 2226 to 2259 (société en commandite / limited partnership), read together with arts. 2186 to 2225 on general partnership contract, and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), arts. 7, 19, 23, 25 and 70 (obligatory registration, declaration contents and registration certificate).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar, RDEQ) — Direction de l'immatriculation.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership (Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2242-2252). Contributions may be in money, property or services as agreed in the partnership contract; no mandatory escrow, capital deposit or bank guarantee is required for a non-licensed mobile software activity conducted under NAICS 511210.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA INITIAL RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER. WHEREAS the limited partnership (société en commandite) was constituted by the Partnership Agreement dated [date] and is to be registered with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; NOW BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) the General Partner subscribes for its general partnership interest, and the admission of the Initial Limited Partner is ratified on the terms of the Contribution Schedule; (2) the registered office is established at [address], Quebec, as shown in the Declaration of Registration; (3) [nominee] is appointed authorized representative of the General Partner with power to file registrations, open bank accounts, execute agreements and manage operations; (4) the authorized representative is instructed to procure the NEQ, GST/QST accounts and municipal permits. Effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability search and reservation before the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (RDEQ) — Online Services / Centre d'affaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the RDEQ online portal (services.registraire.gouv.qc.ca) and launch a name search in the central enterprise register. Verify that the proposed name is distinctive, not misleading, and includes the obligatory legal designation 'société en commandite', 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'. File the name reservation request ('Demande de réservation de nom') indicating NAICS 511210 and the intended software publishing activity. The system issues either a name reservation certificate or a reserved NEQ for the future enterprise.
required_dossiers: Proposed name with mandatory legal designation (L.P. / S.E.C.)
Description of mobile utility software and device performance optimization activities
Identification of the applicant partner
Name search report from the central enterprise register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for lack of distinctiveness or for suggesting a regulated activity, submit written arguments before the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal or amend the name by adding a distinguishing element and file a new demand; notarization is not required at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement and alignment of contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary or corporate law counsel (notarization optional unless immovable contribution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the written Partnership Agreement (contrat de société en commandite) under Civil Code of Québec arts. 2186-2259, designating the general partner (sole manager) and the limited partners; fix contributions in cash or property, profit-sharing ratios, withdrawal, assignment and non-participation clauses limiting the limited partners' management role. If any contribution comprises an immovable, the agreement and its publication must follow notarial deed and land registration formalities.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Schedule of capital contributions and valuation
Identity documents of each partner (individuals: government-issued ID; corporations: registration extract)
Written consent of the general partner to act as manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the contract terms are queried by the Registraire or third parties, execute an amending deed (acte modificatif) correcting the defective clause and file it with the RDEQ; immovable contribution defects are cured by notarized rectification and subsequent land registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — secure electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the standard electronic form 'Déclaration d'immatriculation — société en commandite' on the RDEQ portal using the reserved NEQ. Enter the enterprise name, registered office address in Quebec, date of formation, activity code (NAICS 511210), identification of the general partner and each limited partner, and the amount of each partner's contribution. Attest that the limited partnership is not a legal person and that its object is lawful. Pay the CAD 78 registration fee (approx. USD 57) online; the portal immediately generates the attestation of registration and the enterprise number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Reserved NEQ or name reservation certificate
Extract of the partnership agreement
Identification and address of the general partner and each limited partner
Registered office address in Quebec
Activity declaration for NAICS 511210
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected or queried, correct the flagged elements (consent, address, contribution data) in the RDEQ online file and resubmit within 30 days; the Registraire applies the legal 30-day regularization period before any penalty under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax accounts with Revenu Québec (GST/QST and employer accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec — business registration service via NEQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, register the limited partnership for GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act and for QST under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax through Revenu Québec's secure business registration service. Declare estimated taxable supplies; if employees will work in Quebec, register as an employer for source deductions (income tax, QPIP, CNESST). Select the filing frequency (annual or quarterly) and activate the 'Mon dossier entreprise' online portal.
required_dossiers: NEQ registration certificate
Partnership agreement
Identification and tax numbers of partners (including foreign partners as applicable)
Projected sales volume and payroll estimate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration application is deemed incomplete, supply the missing identification or KYC documents within Revenu Québec's prescribed delay; in case of doubt on taxable status or permanent establishment, request a written ruling; no penalty is applied where corrected documentation is provided within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration governance, banking mandate and municipal clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner / authorized representative; municipality of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the Pro-Forma Initial Resolution of the General Partner; open a segregated partnership bank account using the exact registered name 'société en commandite'; if a physical office or server room is used, obtain a municipal zoning and commercial occupancy certificate consistent with the Quebec Building Code; register the establishment with CNESST if employees are active in Quebec and retain all formation records for the annual update declaration.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma initial resolution of the general partner
Certificate of registration issued by the RDEQ
Lease or ownership title of the registered office
Partner identification and KYC documents for bank onboarding
Municipal occupancy permit application (where a physical office is opened)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal occupancy certificate is refused for zoning reasons, apply for a minor variance before the local zoning committee or relocate the registered office and file a declaration of modification with the RDEQ; banking KYC rejections are cured by supplying a notarized copy of the partnership agreement and the registration certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No Quebec industrial licensing board has competence over ISIC 6201 software publishing. The Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) provides only business support and innovation programs; physical premises, where applicable, are controlled exclusively by municipal urban planning and public security authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — mobile utility application development and distribution is an unlicensed digital service activity in Quebec; the only possible physical requirement is a standard municipal commercial occupancy permit (certificat d'occupation) or zoning clearance for an office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory environmental impact assessment — software development and electronic office operations are not listed in the mandatory EIA categories of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2) and its authorization regulation; no environmental authorization certificate is required for premises below pollutant emission thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Only municipal wastewater, indoor air and residual waste standards apply. Office sanitary effluent must conform to the applicable municipal sewer by-law; no VOC, PM, process wastewater or hazardous industrial discharge limits are triggered by application development, App Store distribution or revenue operations; defective electronic devices and e-waste must be managed under Quebec residual materials policy and extended producer responsibility (REP) programs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: occupancy and safety compliance certificated against the Quebec Building Code and Safety Code (Régie du bâtiment du Québec, RBQ), including smoke detection, fire extinguishers and unobstructed exit paths. Structural clearance: RBQ or municipal inspection required if office load or occupancy exceeds design parameters. Occupational clearance: registration of the establishment with the CNESST, formation of a health and safety program for workplaces with 20 or more workers, first-aid kit provisioning, and a workplace injury prevention notice under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - 'My Business Account' (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html) for federal GST/HST and income tax registration; Revenu Québec - 'CLIC' portal (revenuquebec.ca) for QST, source deductions, and provincial income tax. The Registraire des entreprises du Québec (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) issues the provincial enterprise registration number (NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Quebec limited partnership with non-resident limited partners: (1) determine whether the LP carries on business or has an establishment in Canada/Quebec; (2) file the limited partnership declaration with the Registraire des entreprises and obtain the NEQ; (3) apply to CRA via Form RC1 or Business Registration Online for a Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account, naming the general partner or designated agent as authorized representative; (4) register the QST account with Revenu Québec online or via Form LM-3-V; (5) appoint an agent for service in Quebec if so required. No statutory minimum capital is required; non-resident ownership is permitted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - fiscally transparent for federal and Quebec income tax; each partner reports its proportionate share. For GST/HST and QST, however, the partnership itself is a registrant/person capable of collecting tax and claiming input tax credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election. Available elections include: (i) alternative fiscal-period election under ITA s. 249.1(4); (ii) voluntary GST/HST/QST registration election for small suppliers; (iii) partnership agent election for administrative filings. Hybrid mismatch provisions (ITA ss. 12.1-12.16) reclassify certain dual-status arrangements but cannot elect a limited partnership into a taxable entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST)/Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) administered federally by CRA and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administered provincially by Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (GST/HST and QST small-supplier threshold), measured on worldwide taxable supplies over the current calendar quarter and immediately preceding four calendar quarters; the threshold does not apply where the supply is deemed by law to be made by an online distribution platform operator (Apple/Google).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate exists in Canada. CRA and Revenu Québec accept paper and electronic invoices; registered suppliers must show their BN, tax rate, and tax amount. E-invoices may be issued without prior authorization, but records must be retained for at least six years and a complete audit trail must be available in an electronically readable form.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of software (intangible personal property) and related digital services made to a non-resident recipient for use wholly outside Canada under Schedule VI Part V (GST/HST) and the Quebec Sales Tax Act. For online app store sales, the marketplace operator may be deemed supplier; direct sales to business or consumers are zero-rated only if the LP retains contemporaneous evidence of the recipient's non-residence, the app download jurisdiction is not Canada, the user's location and payment instrument are non-Canadian, and the place of use is outside Canada. Supplies deemed made in Canada are taxable at 14.975% combined.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: App Store Connect/Google Play Console analytical sales and settlement reports identifying storefront, transaction currency, and Apple/Google commission
Contracts or platform terms with Apple/Google showing the LP as principal or supplier of the app and the platform as distribution agent
Digital sales ledger recording each transaction's IP country, device country, bank card country, and storefront code
Bank statements and remittance advices showing the subscription/boxed compensation from Apple/Google received in Canada
GST/QST export reconciliation worksheet listing the zero-rated supplies and the corresponding Schedule VI remission basis
Where tangible media is involved, a customs export declaration and bill of lading; for pure downloads this is not applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA/Revenu Québec may reassess beyond the normal limitation period in cases of neglect or fraud. Falsely zero-rating domestic supplies triggers retroactive GST/QST collection, interest, and penalties: ETA s. 285 gross negligence penalty up to 25% of the tax that should have been collected; ITA s. 163(2) false statements penalty up to 50% of the related income tax understated. Revenu Québec imposes equivalent penalties under the Tax Administration Act, and criminal prosecution applies in egregious cases of tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Banque du Canada; federal foreign exchange regulation is administered by the Department of Finance Canada under the Currency Act, with prudential supervision of Schedule I banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and AML/CFT reporting supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). There is no dedicated Canadian foreign exchange control administration equivalent to an exchange authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full currency convertibility for both current account and capital account transactions under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, interest payments, royalties, loan repayments, and capital repatriation are unrestricted from a foreign exchange standpoint; however, non-resident recipients may be subject to withholding taxes under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and any applicable treaty. No ministerial or central bank pre-approval is required for cross-border transfers of funds into or out of Quebec.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose any statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for receipt or surrender of export proceeds. Exporters may retain payments in foreign currency, maintain foreign-denominated bank accounts domestically or offshore, and are not required to convert such receipts into Canadian dollars. FINTRAC large transaction reporting applies to cash transactions exceeding CAD 10,000, but no exchange conversion requirement exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability. A foreign electronic money institution (EMI) licensed in the EU or UK may offer FX conversion, payment aggregation, and card-wallet settlement in CAD through a sponsored partner arrangement with a Canadian Schedule I bank, but it cannot lawfully take retail deposits or provide full current-account banking services for a Quebec limited partnership. Regulatory constraints include the Bank Act deposit-taking prohibition, Quebec-specific collection and money-services licensing under provincial law, FINTRAC MSB registration, and OSFI guidance on outsourcing. A cross-border EMI may be used solely as an ancillary payment rail, not as the primary account-holding bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Not statutorily mandatory for routine KYC; FINTRAC-compliant clients may undergo an approved video-verified remote onboarding process. However, Canadian chartered banks frequently require at least one authorized signatory or the general partner representative to complete an in-person identity verification or attend a notarized interview, especially for a limited partnership with non-resident limited partners. Physical presence is the practical default for opening a full banking relationship in Quebec, although a tailored video-call and certified-copy package can avoid in-branch attendance for low-risk mobile software exporters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity arising from limited partnership structure, particularly when limited partners are passive non-residents and the general partner is a corporate nominee
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the declaration of registration issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), full partnership agreement, details of all partners and their percentage interests, clear UBO declaration forms, passport copies of all natural-person beneficial owners, corporate registry extracts for corporate general partners, and a signed source-of-funds declaration for each contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mobile app store revenue originating from Apple App Store and Google Play in foreign jurisdictions, combined with a short operating history and high-frequency micro-transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: App store payout reports for at least six months, merchant and developer agreements with Apple and Google, GST/HST and QST registration certificates, app monetization dashboards, audited revenue pipeline statements, and three months of pristine bank statements showing traceability from app store settlements to the operating account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections from overseas parent entities or non-resident limited partners that trigger large-transaction reporting or unexplained deposit alerts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreement or partnership capital contribution agreement, capital account ledger, taxed contribution breakdown, tax residency certificates of contributing partners, SWIFT MT103 evidence showing purpose codes, real-party identification declarations, and a professional accountant’s letter confirming that funds trace to documented, lawful business activities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital contributions are routed from the remitting partner’s bank via SWIFT MT103 to the LP’s CAD settlement account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. The wire should include the partnership’s REQ registration number and the unique reference corresponding to the subscription agreement. Under Statistics Canada’s international transactions reporting, use the applicable balance-of-payments code for direct investment capital injection or other investment liabilities; Canadian banks will apply the appropriate code, such as 'D5 — Other investment — liabilities — capital contributions' or 'P6 — Capital injection into a resident enterprise'. For receipts equal to or above CAD 10,000, FINTRAC large cash transaction reporting rules do not apply to wire transfers, but the bank will apply its own transaction-monitoring thresholds and may request a purpose-of-payment declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 for vendor invoices, software licensing fees, and cloud infrastructure costs. For high-value supply contracts, a commercial letter of credit — typically an irrevocable, confirmed LC drawn under UCP600 — provides safer clearing and protects against documentary non-compliance. Domestic Canadian disbursements use the national EFT clearing system, while cross-border USD payments move through Fedwire via correspondent banks. In-app purchase commission flows to Apple and Google are cleared through the platform-side payment processors and settled back to the LP’s operating account without a separate FX conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (including CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) with authorized Canadian Schedule I or II banks
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY swaps) to manage structural balance-sheet FX exposure between CAD and operational foreign currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to prohibited or restricted-convertibility jurisdictions where domestic forward hedging is impractical

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration for the Quebec limited partnership (Déclaration annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the anniversary date of the partnership’s original declaration of registration; must be refiled every subsequent year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a late fee (CAD 18 to CAD 45 depending on delay); continued failure to file results in the cancellation of the registration and loss of limited liability shield.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and partner allocation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 immediately following the calendar year in which the partnership’s fiscal period ends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day per partner, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500 per return; failure to provide partnership information exposes the general partner to additional fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Information Return (TP-600 plus Relevés 15 if any Quebec resident partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 immediately following the calendar year in which the partnership’s fiscal period ends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of CAD 25 per day per partner, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500 under the Quebec Taxation Act; delinquent registrants may be referred to collection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory external audit is required solely on the basis of revenue or asset thresholds for a Quebec limited partnership. Audit becomes compulsory when the partnership agreement so provides, when any partner holding at least 25% of the partnership shares requests it, or the partnership is a reporting issuer or regulated by certain statutes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For fiscal periods beginning after 2011, non-public enterprises must apply Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) in Canada, while publicly accountable enterprises are required to apply IFRS as published under the CPA Canada Handbook. Quebec resident limited partnerships generally use ASPE.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not require a yearly UBO filing separate from the REQ annual declaration. The declaration confirms the names, residential addresses and ownership percentages of all general and limited partners. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in partner capital must be filed as a modification declaration with REQ within 30 days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (recording contributions, transfers and withdrawals)
Register of General Partner Resolutions (partnership governance and consents)
Minute Book (including the limited partnership agreement and all restated or amended versions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - USD 500 annually for registered office, registered agent and annual record-keeper services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 8,000 annually for a certified accountant’s review or audit of a standard mobile utility app partnership with app-store revenue

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.50% combined federal+Quebec headline corporate rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); the CA_LP itself is fiscally transparent, so no entity-level CIT — each partner is taxed on allocated income at their own marginal rate (Quebec top marginal combined rate 53.31%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED refundable ITC 35% for CCPC partners (first C$3M qualifying expenditures; 15% non-refundable otherwise); Quebec R&D credit 30% (SME) / 14% (large); Quebec refundable multimedia-title tax credit 37.5% (42.5% for qualified SME) on SODEC-certified labour, claimable by qualifying corporate partners; CCPC small business deduction reduces combined rate to 12.2% on first C$500,000 active business income per corporate partner.
